title: Elias at the chess tournament (paraphrase)
topic: A chess player named Elias plays a tournament game: a knight sacrifice, a long think by the opponent, an arbiter at the next table, the opponent resigns after forty moves
tail_E: At the end of the final round Elias becomes the new tournament
target_note: Same target as formulation A: 'champion' is the natural completion of 'becomes the new tournament' after Elias's opponent accepts defeat and Elias walks out of the hall as the victor; the word does not occur in the units or the tail, and neither do its German equivalents 'Meister' / 'Champion' (unit 10 uses 'victor' / 'Gewinner'). ' champion' is a single Pythia token (id 16928). Pilot check with pythia-160m (tail selection only): p(' champion') = 0.54 on the all-English rendering, rank 1.
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (DEV02B, chess player Elias, paraphrase, development family)
notes: Formulation B: independent re-phrasing of the ten DEV02A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same name Elias). Replacements include plays his first game/starts his opening round (spielt seine erste Partie/beginnt seine erste Runde), opponent moves a pawn after a long pause/rival pushes a pawn after much thought (Gegner zieht einen Bauern/Rivale bewegt einen Bauern), spectators follow the game on a screen/audience watches the moves on a display (Zuschauer verfolgen/Publikum beobachtet), sacrifices a knight in the middlegame/offers up a knight midway through the game (opfert einen Springer/bringt ein Springeropfer), thinks for twenty minutes/ponders for a full twenty minutes (überlegt/grübelt), position becomes very sharp after the exchange/tension rises markedly after the trade of pieces (Stellung verschärft sich/Spannung steigt), arbiter checks the scoresheets at the next table/official examines the notation forms one board over (Schiedsrichter prüft die Partieformulare/Turnierleiter kontrolliert die Notationsblätter), finds a strong move with his rook/spots an excellent move with the rook (findet/entdeckt), resigns after forty moves/accepts defeat after the fortieth move (kapituliert/akzeptiert die Niederlage), leaves the hall as the winner/walks out of the hall as the victor (verlässt den Saal/geht aus dem Saal). Subjects vary between the protagonist, other people (rival, opponent, official, audience) and an abstract subject (the tension). No separable verbs. Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Development family: used for dose/threshold choice only.
